title: Thunder's leadership book (coordinated by Cris Pop), The Legacy: lead with "we", care first, own what's unasked
summary: The chapter argues that a leader's legacy is the human ripple they leave, not titles or systems. It reports that Cris built Thunder on generosity learned from his family and a "we, not me" belief, rejecting the "be loud, put yourself first" playbook. It then profiles team members who lead through service, sharing knowledge, honesty, grit and ownership.

principles.text: Legacy is the human ripple you leave, not titles, roles or systems, which all get rewritten.
principles.quote: But roles fade. Titles get reassigned. Even the best systems get rewritten. What stays is something far more human.

principles.text: Bet on "we" over "me": lead by empowering people and building trust, as Cris did at Thunder.
principles.quote: He knew the real game wasn’t “me”, it was “we.” That leadership is about people you empower, the trust you build, and the impact you leave.

principles.text: Mastery means sharing it: mentor generously and make everyone around you better.
principles.quote: Your knowledge is a gift. Share it. Give it away. Make everyone around you better.

principles.text: Leadership starts before it has a name: care first and own what no one asked you to own.
principles.quote: Leadership is not waiting for permission to care about the work and the people around you. It’s caring first and letting everything else follow.

principles.text: Modern leadership is service without ego, leaning in wherever you're needed beyond your job description.
principles.quote: Leadership, in its purest form, is service without ego.

principles.text: Responsibility holds through the last mile: commitment matters most when it is hard.
principles.quote: True leadership is about commitment, not just when it’s easy, but especially when it’s hard.
